stories.title: China extends rare-earth controls worldwide, including to foreign products with 0.1% Chinese content
stories.summary: MOFCOM added five more rare earths (holmium, erbium, thulium, europium, ytterbium) and rare-earth technologies to its controls. It required licences for foreign-made goods containing at least 0.1% Chinese-origin rare earths, with case-by-case review for advanced-chip and military-AI uses. Most measures were due on Nov 8 and Dec 1.

causes.why: Escalates the April regime
Mirrors the extraterritorial reach of US chip rules

analysis.text: Beijing showed it could copy the US foreign-direct-product rule. That gave it the leverage it traded at Busan, and set the Nov 10 2026 cliff.

stories.title: Gaza ceasefire under Trump's plan; all living hostages freed and a Sharm el-Sheikh summit held
stories.summary: The ceasefire took effect at noon on Oct 10 and Israeli forces pulled back to agreed lines. On Oct 13 Hamas freed all 20 living hostages, Israel released nearly 2,000 Palestinian prisoners and detainees, and Trump convened more than 20 leaders in Sharm el-Sheikh.

causes.why: Famine raised pressure on Israel
The Doha backlash pushed Washington to force a deal

stories.title: Venezuela's María Corina Machado wins the Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured Machado for promoting democratic rights and a peaceful transition in Venezuela.
stories.unplaced: Announced in Oslo; no place entity.

stories.title: Madagascar's military seizes power after Gen Z protests; president impeached
stories.summary: After youth protests over water and power cuts, Col. Michael Randrianirina's CAPSAT unit sided with the protesters. President Rajoelina fled and was impeached, and Randrianirina declared a takeover and was sworn in on Oct 17, promising elections within two years.

stories.title: After deadly border clashes, Pakistan and the Taliban agree a Doha ceasefire
stories.summary: After a week of heavy fighting, Qatar- and Turkey-mediated talks in Doha produced an immediate ceasefire. It was extended in Istanbul on Oct 30 with a monitoring mechanism, but later rounds failed to settle the dispute over the TTP.

stories.title: US and Australia sign a critical-minerals framework with an $8.5bn project pipeline
stories.summary: Trump and Albanese signed a framework under which each side commits at least $1bn within six months toward an $8.5bn pipeline of mining and processing projects, plus price floors and faster permitting.

causes.why: Response to China's new controls
Extends the price-floor model to an ally

stories.title: Sanae Takaichi becomes Japan's first woman prime minister
stories.summary: The Diet elected Takaichi with 237 lower-house votes after the LDP formed a coalition with the right-wing Ishin party.
stories.unplaced: A Diet vote; Tokyo has no place entity.

stories.title: Meta's $27bn off-balance-sheet Hyperion financing launches the AI debt era
stories.summary: Meta formed a joint venture with Blue Owl funds, which own 80%, to build its Louisiana Hyperion data centre, financed with about $27bn of debt raised through a separate vehicle. Bloomberg reported Meta and xAI were starting a trend of off-balance-sheet AI debt.

causes.why: The spending race continued despite the scare

stories.title: US sanctions Rosneft and Lukoil
stories.summary: Treasury designated Russia's two largest oil companies and their majority-owned subsidiaries and called on Moscow to agree a ceasefire. Wind-down licences ran to Nov 21.

causes.why: Alaska produced no ceasefire
Deepens the oil sanctions begun in 2022

stories.title: RSF takes El Fasher after an 18-month siege, followed by mass killings
stories.summary: The RSF captured North Darfur's capital. The WHO said about 460 people were killed at the Saudi Hospital. OHCHR later documented more than 6,000 killings on Oct 25–27 and said the violations amount to war crimes.

causes.why: Driven from the capital, the RSF consolidated Darfur

analysis.text: With all of Darfur held, the RSF turned east into Kordofan, toward Babanusa, Kadugli and El Obeid.

stories.title: Busan truce: China suspends its new rare-earth controls for a year and the US cuts tariffs
stories.summary: Trump and Xi met in Busan. Per the White House, China suspended the Oct 9 controls and issued general licences, and the US cut the fentanyl tariff by 10 points and kept its higher reciprocal rates paused until Nov 10 2026. China also committed to soybean purchases.

causes.why: China's new leverage
Unwinds the post-April escalation

analysis.text: This was a truce, not a settlement: both sides' weapons were suspended to Nov 10 2026, which is why that date hangs over today.

stories.title: Supreme Court hears the IEEPA tariff challenge
stories.summary: In Learning Resources v. Trump, consolidated with V.O.S. Selections, the government argued that IEEPA's power to 'regulate importation' covers tariffs. Challengers said tariffs are taxes that need clear congressional approval.

causes.why: The challenged tariffs

stories.title: Takaichi says a Taiwan blockade could be 'survival-threatening', and China retaliates
stories.summary: Takaichi told parliament that a Chinese blockade or attack on Taiwan could be a 'survival-threatening situation', the legal trigger for collective self-defence. Beijing demanded a retraction and warned its citizens against travel to Japan.

causes.why: New hawkish premier

stories.unplaced: Remarks in the Diet; no place entity.

stories.title: USS Gerald R. Ford enters the Caribbean for 'Operation Southern Spear'
stories.summary: The Ford carrier strike group joined the counter-narcotics mission Operation Southern Spear. AP called it a major military build-up near Venezuela.

causes.why: Escalation from boat strikes

stories.title: UN Security Council endorses the Board of Peace and a Gaza stabilisation force
stories.summary: Resolution 2803 passed 13–0, with Russia and China abstaining. It endorsed Trump's comprehensive plan, set up the Board of Peace as a transitional administration, and authorised an International Stabilization Force through 2027.

causes.why: UN backing for the plan

stories.unplaced: Adopted in New York; no place entity.

stories.title: Witkoff–Dmitriev '28-point' Ukraine plan leaks; Geneva talks cut it to 19 points
stories.summary: A US–Russian draft reportedly included territorial concessions, a 600,000-troop cap on Ukraine's army and a permanent bar on NATO membership. After Ukrainian and European pushback, Geneva talks produced a revised 19-point framework without the army cap, while territory stayed unresolved.

causes.why: Follow-on US–Russia channel
Sanctions pressure preceded the push

stories.unplaced: Drafted and negotiated in several capitals.

stories.title: UAE-backed separatists sweep into Hadramawt and Mahra; Saudi Arabia pushes back
stories.summary: The Southern Transitional Council rapidly took much of oil-rich Hadramawt and al-Mahra. Saudi Arabia demanded a withdrawal, which the STC rejected. By late December CSIS reported Saudi strikes near STC forces and on a UAE-linked shipment at Mukalla, and the UAE withdrew counter-terrorism units.

causes.why: The 2022 council papered over Saudi–UAE splits

analysis.text: This brought the Saudi–UAE rivalry into the open. It led straight to the STC's January 2026 dissolution and the UAE's OPEC exit.

stories.title: Tshisekedi and Kagame sign the Washington Accords, and M23 takes Uvira days later
stories.summary: With Trump presiding, the leaders of Congo and Rwanda signed accords requiring Rwanda to withdraw its forces and stop backing armed groups. M23, which did not sign, launched a South Kivu offensive and said it seized Uvira on Dec 10.

causes.why: Peace push after M23's 2025 gains

stories.title: Trump allows Nvidia H200 sales to China in exchange for a 25% cut
stories.summary: Trump said Nvidia could ship H200 AI chips to approved Chinese customers, with 25% of the proceeds going to the US government. Commerce rules followed in January.

causes.why: Chip access as a truce bargaining chip
Loosens the 2022 control regime

stories.title: Fed cuts for a third straight meeting to 3.50–3.75% amid three dissents
stories.summary: The FOMC lowered the target range by 25 basis points, 9–3. Goolsbee and Schmid wanted no cut and Miran wanted a half point. Projections showed one more cut in 2026.

analysis.text: Rates went into 2026 at 3.50–3.75%. The Iran-war oil shock turned the planned easing into Warsh's September 2026 hike.

stories.title: Hard-right José Antonio Kast wins Chile's presidency
stories.summary: Kast beat Jeannette Jara in the runoff with about 58% of the vote, Chile's sharpest shift to the right since the dictatorship.

analysis.text: Part of the swing to the right that carried into Colombia and Brazil in 2026.

stories.title: Trump orders a 'total and complete' blockade of sanctioned tankers serving Venezuela
stories.summary: Trump ordered a blockade of US-sanctioned oil tankers entering or leaving Venezuela,. US forces began pursuing tankers, though Reuters reported Coast Guard capacity limits.

causes.why: Military build-up in place

stories.title: EU leaders agree a €90bn Ukraine loan after the Russian-assets plan collapses
stories.summary: The European Council agreed an interest-free €90bn loan for 2026–27 financed by joint EU borrowing, with Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia opted out. The 'reparations loan' using frozen Russian assets failed over Belgian objections, though the assets stay immobilised.

causes.why: Europe moved to fund Kyiv as the US pressed for concessions
The frozen assets date from 2022

stories.title: Tehran bazaar strikes and protests erupt as the rial hits a record low
stories.summary: Shopkeepers in Tehran's electronics and phone markets closed and protested as the rial fell to about 1.45m per dollar. Protests spread to other markets and cities, and some chants turned against the government.

causes.why: Restored UN sanctions deepened the currency crisis
War damage and isolation
